message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The instructions cover both the **gcloud CLI** (the easiest way) and the **REST API** (if you need to embed it in your own code).

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** is enabled.  
> * You have a **service account** or user credentials with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or the `Editor` role).  
> * You have the **GPU quota** for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in the zone you choose.  
> * The `gcloud` CLI is installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login` or `gcloud auth activate-service-account`).  

---

## 1. Using the gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports A6000 GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-highmem-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 61 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-standard" \
  --maintenance-policy="MIGRATE" \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
  --metadata="install-nvidia-driver=true"   # optional: auto‑install driver
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-highmem-8` gives 8 vCPUs and 61 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1` requests one RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--boot-disk-type` | Persistent disk type (`pd-standard` or `pd-ssd`). |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Keeps the instance running during maintenance events. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU driver installation). |
| `--metadata="install-nvidia-driver=true"` | Optional: tells the NVIDIA driver installer to run automatically on first boot. |

> **Tip**: If you prefer a different machine type (e.g., `n1-standard-16`), just change the value. Just make sure the chosen type supports the GPU you want.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

If you want to embed this in a script or application, you can call the Compute Engine REST API directly.

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "install-nvidia-driver",
        "value": "true"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "maintenancePolicy": "MIGRATE"
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

### Explanation of the JSON fields

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name. |
| `machineType` | Full URL to the machine type. |
| `disks[0]` | Root disk configuration. |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | GPU type and count. |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Passes the `install-nvidia-driver=true` flag to the instance. |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Grants the instance the default service account with full Cloud Platform scope. |
| `maintenancePolicy` | Keeps the instance running during maintenance. |

> **Note**: The `access_token` is short‑lived. In production, use a service account key and the Google Auth Library to obtain a token programmatically.

---

## 3. Verifying the Instance

After creation, you can check that the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="json(accelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```json
"accelerators": [
  {
    "acceleratorCount": 1,
    "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
  }
]
```

Once the instance boots, SSH into it and run:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

## 4. Cleaning Up

When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid incurring charges:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --quiet
```

---

### Quick Reference

| Tool | Command |
|------|---------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create ...` |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/.../zones/.../instances` |

Feel free to adjust the machine type, disk size, or zone to fit your workload. Happy GPU computing!
